We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a para-methyl phenyl sulfonamide attached to a phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (anilide). So overall: p-tolyl-sulfonyl attached to a phenyl ring which has a side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH (anilide). Actually the side chain is an α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (c3ccccc3N). So the amide nitrogen is attached to an aniline (anilide). So the target can be disconnected into three steps:

1. Disconnection of amide bond: break C(=O)-N (amide) to give carboxylic acid (α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). This matches the guidance: carboxylic acid to amide via coupling. So retrosynthesis: target -> amide precursor: α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (trans- cinnamic acid derivative) + aniline.

The α,β-unsaturated acid is: c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2 attached to sulfonyl? Wait the sulfonyl is attached to the phenyl ring (c2ccc(... )cc2). The side chain attaches to that phenyl at para position? Actually SMILES: ...c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the phenyl ring (c2) has the side chain at one position (maybe para to sulfonyl). So the acid would be: c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2 (cinnamic acid attached to phenyl). So step 1: break amide to give cinnamic acid (with phenyl) and aniline.

2. Disconnection of the C=C double bond formation via Doebner modification: break the double bond to give aromatic aldehyde (benzaldehyde derivative) and malonic acid (or its derivative). The forward reaction: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated acid. So retrosynthesis: cinnamic acid -> aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl ring with aldehyde) + malonic acid (or maybe malonic acid derivative). The aldehyde would be the same phenyl ring (c2ccc(CHO)cc2). So step 2: break C=C to give p-sulfonyl phenyl aldehyde.

3. Disconnection of sulfonamide formation: break S-N bond to give sulfonyl chloride (or sulfonic acid) and aniline (the p-tolyl amine). Actually the sulfonamide is between the p-tolyl amine (p-methyl aniline) and sulfonyl attached to phenyl ring. The forward reaction: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide. So retrosynthesis: sulfonamide -> p-toluidine (p-methyl aniline) + aryl sulfonyl chloride (the phenyl sulfonyl chloride). The phenyl sulfonyl chloride is derived from the phenyl ring (c2) with sulfonyl chloride at para position relative to aldehyde? In SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... )cc2. So the sulfonyl chloride would be ClS(=O)(=O)-c2ccc(??)cc2? Actually the sulfonyl is attached to the p-tolyl amine via N, and attached to phenyl ring via S. So the sulfonyl chloride precursor would be the phenyl sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph). So step 3: break S-N to give p-toluidine and phenyl sulfonyl chloride.

Thus we have three steps: (1) amide formation, (2) Doebner modification, (3) sulfonamide formation.

Now we need to find appropriate template IDs for each step. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria with appropriate functional groups.

Step 1: amide formation (forward: carboxylic acid + amine -> amide). In retrosynthesis we need template that breaks amide to acid + amine. So functional groups broken: amide (maybe "amide" is broken) and formed: aliphatic carboxylic acid? Actually forward forms amide, breaks carboxylic acid. In retrosynthesis we break amide to acid + amine. So we need template where functional_groups_broken includes "amide" and functional_groups_formed includes "aliphatic carboxylic acid". Let's search.
